items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S913

SPONSOR: YOUNG
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the highway law, in relation to designating a portion of
the state highway system as the "Lance Corporal Aaron M. Swanson Memori-
al Highway"

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

Designates State Route 394 in the Village of Lakewood, County of Chau-
tauqua, as the "Lance Corporal Aaron M. Swanson Memorial Highway."

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends the highway law by adding a new section 344-h, which
designates State Route 394 in the Village of Lakewood, county of Chau-
tauqua, as the "Lance Corporal Aaron M. Swanson Memorial Highway."

Section 2: States that the commissioner of transportation shall provide
for the installation and maintenance of adequate signing of the state
highway systems as designated pursuant to section 1 of this act. The
designation will be for ceremonial purposes only, and the roads official
name will not be changed as a result of this act.

Section 3: Provides that the act shall take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Lance Corporal Aaron M. Swanson served his nation in Afghanistan
assigned to the United States Marine's 3rd Battalion, 25th Marine Regi-
ment, 4th Marine Division, Marine Forces Reserve, Buffalo, New York.
Lance Corporal Swanson tragically lost his life in service to our coun-
try on February 7, 2011 while conducting combat operations in Garmsir
District, Helmand Province, Afghanistan.

Lance Corporal Swanson was a native of Lakewood, New York, a graduate of
Southwestern High School in Jamestown, and attended Jamestown Community
College prior to serving in the Marines. The Chautauqua County Legisla-
ture has expressed its desire to honor Lance Corporal Swanson. The Chau-
tauqua County Legislature, by unanimous vote, adopted a formal resol-
ution requesting this legislation. The dedication of State Route 394 in
the Village of Lakewood is but one small way for this state to honor the
bravery, dedication and ultimate sacrifice of this brave American hero.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2018: S.8854/A.10973 Passed Senate

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
